_doc: Cross-language drift guard for the estate's CLUB-ENGINE mirrors (normalization item 2): audiobook_catalog's browser-side site/club-reads.js (the canon — it is what the live app runs) and its Python announcer app/club_announcements.py, which hand-ports the schedule-position maths and the two tally functions so the unattended Discord bot can compute the same numbers without a browser. Both live in ONE repo (audiobook_catalog) but are two runtimes with no shared code, which is exactly how the estate's other cross-language bugs started (see title-key-fixtures.json's header). The UNIVERSES mechanism, applied a third time.
_measured: Every 'expectPosition' / 'expectStatus' / 'expect' value below was produced by executing site/club-reads.js through vitest on 2026-08-14 (the real browser-side module, not hand-computed) — that file is the canon. If a case here looks wrong, the fix is in whichever side disagrees with club-reads.js, never an edit to this file.
_divergenceFound2026_08_14: Building this fixture file caught a REAL bug, not a hypothetical one: app/club_announcements.py's member_position(milestones, progress) took no `chaptered` argument at all and INFERRED it from whether any milestone carried `chEnd` — a different signal than memberSchedulePosition's explicit `chaptered` parameter (JS sources it from hasChapters(), i.e. read.chapterTitles.length > 0). The two signals are set atomically together at read creation in production (site/club-reads.js:startRead stamps both from the same object in one write), so the bug was invisible for every read the live app has ever created — but the two ADVERSARIAL cases below, where an explicit chaptered disagrees with milestone shape, reproduced a genuine numeric divergence from canon: position 1 vs 0 in one direction, -1 vs 2 in the other (verified against the pre-fix code before landing the change; see the two 'ADVERSARIAL' cases in positionCases). FIXED same day: member_position now takes an optional explicit `chaptered` parameter (defaulting to the old inference for backward compatibility), and on_track_summary/build_embed now pass bool(read.get('chapterTitles')) explicitly, matching hasChapters() exactly. See app/club_announcements.py's member_position docstring for the full account.

memberSchedulePosition / member_position: audiobook_catalog app/club_announcements.py — member_position(milestones, progress, chaptered=None) — chaptered now explicit, see _divergenceFound2026_08_14 above
scheduleStatus / hasSchedule: audiobook_catalog site/club-reads.js — scheduleStatus(milestones, progress, chaptered, nowMs) + hasSchedule(milestones) (canon)

audiobook_catalog app/club_announcements.py — NO literal per-member mirror exists. on_track_summary() computes the same behindBy count via past_due_positions()+member_position() and aggregates it across all members into an 'N of M on track' string rather than a per-member status enum. tests/test_club_fixtures.py composes past_due_positions+member_position itself, from the SAME statusCases fixtures, to assert the primitives Python actually has reproduce canon's behindBy/status for one member at a time — it does not invent a new production function to test against.
tallyRatings / tally_ratings: audiobook_catalog app/club_announcements.py — tally_ratings(ratings) -> (average, count) — same values, tuple instead of an object
tallyPollVotes / tally_poll_votes: audiobook_catalog site/club-reads.js — tallyPollVotes(options, votes) -> { counts, total } (canon)

audiobook_catalog app/club_announcements.py — tally_poll_votes(options, votes) -> counts (list only; Python derives 'any votes at all' from any(counts) in poll_winners() instead of carrying a separate total field — a shape difference, not a logic divergence)

_runners: audiobook_catalog — python -m pytest tests/test_club_fixtures.py (reads catalog-platform/data/ directly, same SKIP-not-fail posture as tests/test_universes.py when the sibling checkout is absent)
